meta.title: Noctua Iosevka — a monospace for terminals, editors and code
meta.description: Noctua Iosevka is a custom build of Iosevka: 135 real faces in nine weights, five widths and three slopes, {sets} named stylistic sets, {variants} character variants and a Nerd Font twin for the terminal. Free under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
meta.og_title: Noctua Iosevka — 135 real faces of one monospace
meta.og_description: Nine weights, five widths, three slopes, {sets} stylistic sets and a Nerd Font twin. A custom build of Iosevka, free under the SIL OFL 1.1.

nav.label: Sections
hero.lede: A monospace for terminals, editors and code. Nine weights, five widths, three slopes — every one a real face, none of them synthesized.
hero.hint: Move across the title — the weight follows you
about.title: Not a fork. Nothing redrawn.
about.statement: Noctua Iosevka is a deliberate selection among the glyph variants Iosevka already offers, plus a remapped width ladder. Its Normal width is 600 units — the same 0.6 em advance as JetBrains Mono — so every glyph has room to be itself.
about.plan_spacing: Symbols are narrowed to the terminal cell, and the ligatures stay in the file as an optional OpenType feature that each application can switch off.
about.plan_cvss: The character variants and the stylistic sets are exported, so any OpenType-aware editor can swap shapes while you work.
about.plan_names: Glyph names survive in the file — what the Nerd Fonts patcher, and terminals such as kitty, rely on.
faces.title: 135 faces. Zero synthesis.
faces.lede: 9 weights × 5 widths × 3 slopes. Every coordinate is its own file, and the browser is never allowed to fake a bold or a slant.
faces.lede_pick: Pick one and the stage switches to that exact face.
faces.stage_line: Sphinx of black quartz, judge my vow.
faces.scan_on: Scanning the family — hover, click or use the arrow keys to take over
faces.wall_title: The whole family on one sheet
faces.wall_hint: — every tile is a real file; choose one to put it on the stage. Arrow keys move through the sheet.
faces.wall_hint_static: — every tile is a real file, set in its own face.
faces.readout_title: Read from the face’s own tables
widths.title: Five widths, one honest ladder.
widths.lede: Stock Iosevka is famously narrow. Here Normal is 600 units — JetBrains Mono’s 0.6 em — and the other four rungs map honestly onto the CSS width classes: condensed, semi-condensed, semi-expanded, expanded.
widths.note: The faint grid under each line is drawn in ch units. In a monospace one ch is exactly one cell, so the ladder measures itself.
slopes.title: Upright, oblique, italic.
slopes.caption: Oblique printed over Italic. Where the inks coincide the shapes agree; where they part, the italic has drawn its own letter.
slopes.lede: Both slanted faces lean {slant}°. The oblique is the roman, slanted. The italic is the same slant with cursive letters where it counts. It redraws, among others, C c e i t and ß æ œ ſ in Latin, ε ι τ ϲ in Greek, and in Cyrillic the capitals С Є and most of the lowercase — а в г д е и й п с т у ф ц ш щ ъ ы ь. Accented letters follow their base letter, and some symbols, such as ¢ © €, change too. In all, {italic_redrawn} of the {codepoints} code points differ; the rest are shared with the oblique.
legibility.title: Every *confusable*, settled by shape.
legibility.lede: The acceptance set: at any size and in all three slopes, no character here may be mistaken for its neighbour. Below, each pair is printed twice on the same spot, in two inks — wherever the colours separate, the letters differ.
legibility.p_0O: Oval zero with a long dot inside; it never meets Ø or ∅.
legibility.p_1l: The one has serifs at the top and the foot; the l ends in a flat tail.
legibility.p_Il: A serifed capital I against the tailed l.
legibility.p_lbar: The bar stays a bar: no serif, no tail.
legibility.p_Z2: The Z carries a horizontal crossbar.
legibility.p_5S: A flat-topped five against an S with one serif.
legibility.p_8B: A crossing eight against a B with serifs on both sides.
legibility.p_QO: The Q’s tail crosses the bowl and curls away.
legibility.p_g9: A single-storey g with a flat hook against the round nine.
legibility.p_rnm: The m carries a tail, so r n never reads as m.
legibility.matter_caption: The same glyphs sampled into a three-ink dot screen: each dot is a pixel of the real outline. It cycles through the confusables.
legibility.small_hint: Point at a line: a 6× loupe redraws it at your screen’s pixel density, up to 2×.
owl.title: Interlude: an owl set in the font
owl.caption: is drawn with nothing but the font — half blocks, shades, box drawing and Braille. No image, no SVG.
sets.title: {sets} alter egos, named in the font.
sets.lede: The build exports Iosevka’s stylistic sets, ss01 to ss20 (there is no ss19). Each one dresses the same letters as another classic monospace, and its name comes straight from the font’s name table.
sets.lede_lens: Move the lens over the text to preview a set — the title above wears it too; wear it to set this page’s running text in it.
sets.lede_static: The lens over the sample and the title above show {set_default}, the set that redraws the most.
sets.lens_label: A lens that shows the sample text in the chosen stylistic set
sets.lens_help: Pointer: move over the text. Keyboard: focus the panel and use the arrow keys. Choose a card below to load its set into the lens; each card prints the letters the set redraws over the default ones, which show through in pink.
sets.wear_none: The page is set in Noctua Iosevka’s own shapes.
cv.title: {variants} dials, one glyph at a time.
cv.lede: Below the stylistic sets sit the character variants, cv01 to cv99: one feature per letter, and each value picks one of its shapes. The counts come from the font itself. One value always reproduces the default glyph, so “{first_shapes} shapes” means {first_shapes} distinct outlines, the default among them.
lig.title: Ligatures that keep to the grid.
lig.lede: Operators join through calt, which browsers, and terminals such as Ghostty and kitty, switch on by default; editors such as VS Code need it enabled (see the settings under Download). dlig joins more of them, and HSKL joins Haskell’s not-equal. Every joined glyph still fills exactly the cells its characters would — the grid underneath proves it.
lig.note: Sequences such as &&, ** and += are left alone by design. Under each joined form, in hexadecimal: the code points it is made of.
lig.note_langs: HSKL is one of several language-tuned ligature sets the font carries as features of their own — RAKU, MLXX, PURS, ELMX, ERLA, JLIA, SWFT and more.
code.title: Code, in five languages.
code.lede: Comments fall into the italic, keywords into the bold, and the ligatures do their quiet work. The colouring is written by hand: no highlighter runs on this page.
code.rs_c1: Parse a hex colour such as "#0b0a10" into its three channels.
code.rs_c2: Fails on anything that is not two hex digits per channel.
code.ts_c1: Run `fn` once the calls have stopped for `ms` milliseconds.
code.ts_c2: Log the window size at most once per burst of resizes.
code.py_c1: Count the confusable characters in a file — a tiny legibility audit.
code.go_c1: tail follows a file the way `tail -f` does, line by line.
code.hs_c1: The width ladder of Noctua Iosevka, in units per em.
code.hs_c2: Each width as a fraction of the em.
term.title: Every icon, exactly one cell.
term.lede: The twin family, NoctuaIosevka Nerd Font Mono, bakes in every Nerd Fonts icon, each one cell wide — so prompts, file listers and status bars line up on the grid like everything else.
term.aria: A terminal set in NoctuaIosevka Nerd Font Mono: a Powerline prompt with icons, btop graphs in Braille inside box-drawn panels with an icon beside each process, fastfetch with an owl drawn in half blocks, and a tmux status line.
term.fs_label: The terminal family string, character for character
term.fs_note: Confirm it with fc-match: a misspelt name fails silently and hands you another font.
term.icons_label: A few of the Nerd Fonts icons in the twin family

tester.title: Your text, any face.
tester.lede_controls: Every control here maps onto a real face or a real OpenType feature, and a face is fetched only when you ask for it.
tester.lede_static: Here your text stays in the Regular, with the default features; choosing another face or feature takes JavaScript.
tester.sample: Sphinx of black quartz, judge my vow.
dl.title: Download & install.
dl.lede: Release {tag} ships one archive per width and format, each with its licences inside. Start with Normal; for the terminal, take the Nerd Font build.
dl.linux_1: Unpack the archive into your own font folder — no root needed.
dl.linux_2: Refresh the font cache, then confirm the exact family name.
dl.linux_3: On NixOS or Guix, point the package manager at the files instead of copying them into $HOME: a copy works, but the next rebuild that prunes the profile takes it away.
dl.mac_2: Open the .ttf files with Font Book, or put them in ~/Library/Fonts/:
dl.mac_3: Quit and reopen your terminal or editor completely.
dl.win_2: Select every .ttf file, right-click and choose Install for all users (or Install).
dl.win_3: Restart the application: many programs look for fonts only when they start.
dl.cfg_title: Then tell your terminal or editor:
dl.cfg_emacs: Every frame takes it, the ones emacsclient opens included. In a terminal, emacs -nw draws with the terminal’s font.
dl.cfg_neovim: For a graphical front end such as Neovide. In a terminal, Neovim draws with the terminal’s font: set that one above.
dl.cfg_note: If the font does not show up, make sure the process really ended — single-instance apps stay alive with every window closed — before suspecting anything else.
